Name: Antguzzler
Trivia: If you've ever wished anteaters were spikier, this is the monster for you. It uses its long tongue to slurp army ants right out of their colonies.

Name: Armoured Wartoise
Trivia: Terrifying tortoises with spiky metallic shells. Try swinging a sword at one and you'll draw back a broken blade. Fortunately, they're also veeeeeery sloooooow.

Name: Avian Android
Trivia: Winged killers originally constructed as tools of interrogation. They probe for the truth using highly focused sound waves, coupled with the hypnotic effect of their multicoloured feathers.

Name: Bad Apple
Trivia: These juicy jokers are bad for anyone's health. While growing in underworld orchards, they're individually bagged to keep insectoid monsters at bay.

Name: Bad Egg
Trivia: These unhatched eggs are yet to make their mark on monsterdom, but were laid with limitless potential to succeed. Their greatest fear is turning out to be a flightless bird.

Name: Bambooligan
Trivia: Clockwork contraptions modelled on killing machines but built from bamboo to keep construction costs down.

Name: Bantamweight
Trivia: These colossal chickens somehow learned to fly. With biceps buffed for the boxing ring, they can deliver a K.O. worthy of a professional pugilist.

Name: Bludgerigar
Trivia: These plump parrots are at their most delicious when they're all bulked up for the winter. Bake in an oven for best results.

Name: Bodkin Archer
Trivia: These cautious creatures are always ready to loose an arrow from the shadows. Sadly, when it comes to matters of the heart, they always seem to miss their mark...

Name: Bongo Drongo
Trivia: Strapping spirits in thrall to their demonic bongos. All manner of monsters are drawn to their deft drumming, entranced by the intricate rhapsody of rhythm.

Name: Boppin' Badger
Trivia: Who can resist this trickster's ballooning belly or the lustrous leaf it wields? A versatile shapeshifter, it delights in playing pranks on unsuspecting adventurers.

Name: Box Slime
Trivia: Satisfyingly squidgy to the touch, these former bubble slimes settled inside treasure chests for so long they solidified into charming cuboids.

Name: Bubble Slime
Trivia: These unfortunate creatures were once normal slimes until permeated by swamp poison that made their bodies collapse like underbaked meringue.

Name: Buddy Slime
Trivia: Slimes that were so fond of eating their greens they sprouted leaves of their own. Now they soak up sunshine and satisfy their energy needs through photosynthesis instead.

Name: Bullfinch
Trivia: Evolutionary pressures shaped these once-harmless birds into bovoid bipeds that incandesce with ire at any suggestion they might be chicken.

Name: Bunicorn
Trivia: Protruding form the noggin of this rabbit-like monster is a single pointy horn. On lonely nights, it huddles with its brethren, everyone taking great care not to move their heads too much.

Name: Burr Baby
Trivia: These volatile vermin are made of gunpowder and love to play pranks. A single touch is all it takes for them to start the countdown to detonation<--->just watch the panic ensue.

Name: Cactiball
Trivia: These smiley succulents are all but indistinguishable from their not-so-sentient cactus cousins, but only when asleep.

Name: Candy Cat
Trivia: These carefree kitties are beloved by some for their trademark lolling tongues and stripy coats. Their fur is delightfully fluffy, but petting them can be a health hazard.

Name: Cannibox
Trivia: Tricksters that pretend to be treasure chests to spring sneak attacks on unsuspecting travellers. They absolutely will not stand for running away<--->try too hard to flee and they'll really flip their lid.

Name: Cannonbrawler
Trivia: Their ships sunk, these salty seafarers are trying to regain their land legs. The urge to roam remains strong for some, who dream of traversing the world on the back of their trusty cannons.

Name: Capsichum
Trivia: These vile vegetal dizygotes have been joined at the hip since birth with a skewer. Constantly butting heads, they are usually encountered mid-quarrel.

Name: Cauldragon
Trivia: Poisonous creatures that ingest all manner of toxicants to keep predators at bay. Their venom varies in effect depending on what disgusting diet they're on, which is usually so unhealthy that a sip of pure spring water will actually upset their stomachs.

Name: Coconut Slime
Trivia: These hirsute handfuls have a habit of finding their way into actual coconut crops. They even contain a kind of milk, though it's far too viscous for human consumption.

Name: Crabid
Trivia: These monsters hunt their prey in squadrons with deadly decapodal discipline. When evening falls, they heed the orders of their top brass and sidle back to their barracks.

Name: Crested Viper
Trivia: If this expressive serpent likes you, it'll spread its crest to show off; if not, it'll spread its crest to warn you off. You have to admire its commitment to the cresty bit.

Name: Croc-a-Bugle-Doo
Trivia: These brassy beasts toot their own horns loud and proud. Their spiffy tunes entice their crocodilian chums out to march in time, bringing traffic to a standstill.

Name: Cruelcumber
Trivia: Spawned when an evil spirit inhabits a leftover cucumber, these monsters are a cautionary tale about picky eating. Despite their skill with a spear, they are known to skewer themselves after taking a tumble.

Name: Cumaulus
Trivia: These puffs of living vapour often get lost on blustery days after powerful gusts carry them far from home.

Name: Cyclown
Trivia: A wicked wind spirit dressed in a dandy dust devil. It lives to lure adventurers into its wonderful whirling world.

Name: Damselfly
Trivia: These dragons like to ensorcell travellers with their beautiful fairy wings. Not only bewitching to behold, their wings also release a fine powder which puts their prey in a trance.

Name: Dancing Devil
Trivia: These prancing princelings are monsterkind nobility and take the top spot at every dance-off they enter.

Name: Dessert Demon
Trivia: These sweet-tempered devils dislike disputes and disagreements<--->they'd rather use their giant spoons for consuming masses of ice cream than combat.

Name: Dracky
Trivia: These nocturnal nuisances emerge from the caves at night to stretch their wings. They love nothing more than slurping on human blood<--->the fresher, the better, so watch out, kids!

Name: Drag Racer
Trivia: Dragons that use their powerful hind legs to propel themselves forward and dish out high-speed headbutts. One of the quickest monsters around<--->at full pelt, you won't see them for dust.

Name: Dragonthorn
Trivia: Cursed thickets of thorns tangled into draconic forms. Anyone entwined in their vicious vines is soon drained of life, leaving nothing but a withered husk behind.

Name: Drake Slime
Trivia: These orange slimes love dragons so much they've sculpted their own bodies into imitations of their idols. They long to grow up to be fully fledged dragons.

Name: Drakularge
Trivia: These corpulent dragons are so vast as to be oft mistaken for minor hillocks. Said to carry their hoards of gold wherever they go, hidden somewhere upon their person.

Name: Dread Squirrel
Trivia: These adorable rodents use their detachable tails as pillows when they bed down for the night.

Name: Drohl Drone
Trivia: Mysterious creatures quite unlike any other found in nature. Classified as monsters largely for their propensity for pouncing upon people.

Name: Eggsoskeleton
Trivia: Mysterious creatures who pilot ovoid war machines capable of vaulting leaps. What they really look like inside that thing is anyone's guess.

Name: Erazor Blade
Trivia: These monsters come to life when sinful souls settle in sabres which travellers have left for scrap. The blades are impeccably maintained, their sharpness visible in every sinister sparkle.

Name: Ethereal Serpent
Trivia: These golden dragons, said to hail from the distant east, like to drift dreamily above the clouds.

Name: Fat Rat
Trivia: Rotund rodents that like to lurk in the same dark, dank caves and sewers as their regular-sized ratty relatives.

Name: Feral Slime
Trivia: These slimes are adapted to life in the unforgiving rainforest. Hardened survivors, they do whatever it takes to escape predators, be it holding their breath in muddy water or climbing to the highest reaches of the canopy.

Name: Feralball
Trivia: This fluffball is covered in green fur from top to toe and is easily spooked. But before it scarpers, those with sharp eyes might spot something odd where this beastie's nose should be...

Name: Firespirit
Trivia: No-one knows for certain how these monsters came to be. Some believe they were born of a fiery Frizz spell, while others think they are the souls of those who died with a burning desire for revenge.

Name: Flython
Trivia: Supersized serpents that have evolved huge hoodlike cowls. When the moon is full, they can be spotted high above the ocean waves, soaring on outstretched frills.

Name: Foo Dog
Trivia: Vicious canines that serve as guard dogs in the netherworld. Other monsters are all too wary of these unpleasant pooches, probably because of their insatiable bloodlust.

Name: Fright Bulb
Trivia: These vegetable monsters simply sprouted from the earth one day. Their shrieks are said to root anyone who hears them to the spot.

Name: Fromage Fray
Trivia: Infamous fondue-filching fiends who are hell-bent on devouring all the dairy they can. No matter how much provolone they pack away, these inveterate dine-and-dashers never seem to get a stitch when cheesing it from the scene of the crime.

Name: Funghoul
Trivia: Great big gurning mushrooms that sprout together in damp conditions. They send travellers to sleep with soporific spores, then use the snoozing bodies as living beds to propagate their offspring.

Name: Funky Ferret
Trivia: After luring in prey with their Sweet Breath, these fiendish furballs wait till their quarry is nodding off before eating them whole. This eye-catching approach to hunting has been celebrated in lays by bards of high renown.

Name: Gasbagon
Trivia: Dragons which float using gas trapped in their bellies. Best kept away from open flames, they are nevertheless capable of breathing fire, which is both dangerous and deflating for them.

Name: Ghost
Trivia: These sad souls died bearing the heavy regret of unfinished business. They're always trying to scare the living one way or another, just for the attention.

Name: Gloomy Grublin
Trivia: Innocent-looking imps that roam the grasslands. Often found weeping over boo-boos incurred by tripping over their own feet.

Name: Gold Golem
Trivia: Silent servants of solid gold. Not to be confused with the storefront statues modelled after them, which are popular among merchants as symbols of wealth.

Name: Goonache Goodie
Trivia: Alluring aromas enticed these hapless chocoslimes to poke their heads into a pastry pocket, whereupon they found themselves firmly stuck.

Name: Great Sabrecub
Trivia: The offspring of a great sabrecat. If taken in at an early age and lavished with care and affection, they can be tamed and kept as pets.

Name: Greater Dracky
Trivia: These gentle giants are the physical elite of drackykind, capable of crushing all comers. As kind as they are huge, they're always looking out for their smaller kin.

Name: Gremlin
Trivia: These maddening monsters live to make fun of humans. Even on their last legs they'd rather take the mickey than beg for mercy.

Name: Guaardvark
Trivia: These crazed creatures love to collect human crania, and take their favourite specimen wherever they go.

Name: Hammerhood
Trivia: These bushy bashers wield mallets as big as they are. Each one is artisanally crafted by family members<--->a small comfort, perhaps, to the foes they flatten.

Name: Hangelabra
Trivia: These demons swing from the ceiling, sizing up their prey. Their sticking power was thought to be sorcery, but recent research has shown that it's simply raw strength.

Name: Healslime
Trivia: These soft-hearted slimes simply cannot stand by when they spy someone in need. Word has it there's one in particular who travels far and wide to pursue his dream of becoming human.

Name: Hellbound Horror
Trivia: These hooded half-pints seem to like making their own lives difficult, given how tightly they've tied themselves to their spiky stakes.

Name: Hunter Mech
Trivia: Merciless mechs made to hunt metallic monsters. Fed up with their quick and cowardly quarry, they long to be upgraded to killing machines.

Name: Icy Dragling
Trivia: Darling little dragons who could easily pass as pixies. Their favourite food (if you could call it that) is solid ice, but their tender tummies can't take too much.

Name: Imp
Trivia: These little devils carry the future of the underworld upon their shoulders. Desperate to be seen as grown-up, they're always trying to cast spells they're not yet big or bad enough to pull off.

Name: Jargon
Trivia: These chaps will shove anything and everything into their beloved jars<--->pickles, preserves, jams, chutneys...even the occasional weapon.

Name: Jingle Bug
Trivia: These oversized insects ring in the autumn. Their tintinnabulations may sound sweet to the ear, but make it difficult for them to flee from predators.

Name: Khalamari Kid
Trivia: These squid-like squirts are baby khalamari. Though small in stature, they're as tough as any full-grown sea-dweller.

Name: Killer Gila
Trivia: These lumpy lizards sport slick, slippery scales that are powerfully poisonous. Their deepest desire is to slip into a bath of bubble slime foam.

Name: Killerpillar
Trivia: Despite their larval look, these creepy-crawlies are fully grown. On cold days, they curl up tight in an attempt to stay snug and warm.

Name: King Kelp
Trivia: Despite their regal nature, these monsters love nothing more than gathering the gang to belt out bawdy ballads. It's no wonder they're so cherished by their subjects<--->they always sing from the heart.

Name: Kingfuschia
Trivia: These unusual avians feed on the bugs that visit their flower-like faces. When predators approach, they pose as a posies and pray for the best.

Name: Komodo
Trivia: Nippy little dragons with highly developed hind legs. At full pelt, they can outpace a racehorse, but are yet to master the subtle art of slowing down.

Name: Lampling
Trivia: These fiery fiends inhabit lanterns discarded by their owners. They like to terrify unfortunate adventurers who tramp their terrain at night.

Name: Leafy Larrikin
Trivia: Fiery foliage with a melancholy autumnal streak, resembling, as they do, reddening leaves fluttering on the breeze. Their unhappiness is fuelled by their struggle to put on all that footwear each morning.

Name: Lips
Trivia: Who could resist a king-sized smooch from one of these luscious lumps? These full-lipped fiends are protective of their prime assets<--->you won't catch one without their trusty lip balm.

Name: Little Devil
Trivia: A child from hell training in the overworld in order to join the upper ranks of devilry. Its love of mischief<--->and delight in human vexation<--->suggests great things in its future.

Name: Lump Wizard
Trivia: These baggy blobs were once mighty mages, but in their blinkered pursuit of sorcery's secrets they let themselves dwindle to the woebegone wodges you see now.

Name: Lunatick
Trivia: These curious creatures comprise an enormous eyeball that affords excellent vision, even in absolute darkness. Once they set their sights on their prey, they don't stop until it's tangled up in their tentacles.

Name: Mad Moai
Trivia: These undead heads of giants remember the pain of decapitation, and are still angry about it, as their permanent scowl reveals.

Name: Mad Mollusk
Trivia: These monsters have two mouths, one at each end. The one at the front is a strict vegetarian, while the one on the tail is proudly carnivorous.

Name: Marislime
Trivia: When a careless slime fell into the sea, it was sink or swim<--->fortunately, some friendly fish were around to show it the ropes. Evolution eventually gave it the ability to stay underwater for extended periods without dissolving a bit.

Name: Mecha-Mynah
Trivia: Adorable clockwork avians made by monsters to monitor mankind. Tragically, their inner mechanisms are too heavy to perch on a branch without breaking it.

Name: Merman
Trivia: The scourge of fishing villages the world over, these half-fish sea-dwellers often sally to the surface to test their strength against anyone they encounter.

Name: Midnight Horknight
Trivia: These mischief-loving gloomy grublins have mastered the art of wasp-riding. Rank within their knightly clans is determined by size alone<--->the size of their wasps, that is.

Name: Mischievous Mole
Trivia: These tunnelling tricksters always carry a shovel to dig traps for unsuspecting travellers...or so we all thought. Of late, they've begun to show more interest in burrow renovations than playing petty pranks.

Name: Mitey Oak
Trivia: These infant tree spirits are a lovely shade of acorn brown. They grow up hale and hearty, surrounded by doting meadowland monsters.

Name: Molten Slime
Trivia: These slimes are permanently on the brink of boiling over. Urban legend claims that if you chill one for long enough it turns into a regular blue slime, but no one has ever attempted the experiment.

Name: Monolog
Trivia: Not only can this tree trunk terror fly, it can even disguise itself as a common or garden tree stump. You can hardly blame stump chumps for feeling rather supplanted.

Name: Mottle Slime
Trivia: Every one of these timid creatures sports a unique pattern of spots. Sadly, they're too terrified of their own shadows to show them off.

Name: Mouldfish
Trivia: These putrefied piscines swim in the underworld's stagnant waters. The rare specimen that ends up in a fishing net on the surface fetches a pretty price or its rarity. Delicious fried, if you dare.

Name: Mud Mannequin
Trivia: These models were sculpted from mud and brought to life with magic. To compensate for their inexpressive faces, they articulate their feelings through the medium of dance.

Name: Muddy Hand
Trivia: Monsters that lurk beneath mud and murk, leaving only a hand wholly visible. Run into one and you can expect more than just a slap on the wrist.

Name: Mudraker
Trivia: Spirits of the dead who dwell in mud, glorious mud and fear nothing more than clement weather. The sun's vicious rays can bake them solid, causing their sense of self to crumble.

Name: Mummy Boy
Trivia: An ancient king who believed he would be revived after his death and had his body preserved for the occasion. Alas, dark magic somehow seeped into his cadaver and turned him into this sorry swaddled sight.

Name: Napir
Trivia: Mean-spirited mammalian monsters that sustain themselves by devouring dreams. Though every dream is downright delectable to them, nothing nourishes like a good nightmare.

Name: Nardragon
Trivia: These warlike wyrms are armed with wicked horns. Their courtship rituals are highly hazardous affairs in which the clash of horn on horn sets the rhythm to their pre-nuptial dance.

Name: Odd Cob
Trivia: Diabolical cobs of corn. Toasting their kernels over a medium flame produces an odd-tasting but perfectly palatable popcorn...or so the rumours go.

Name: Onion Slime
Trivia: Slimes which overindulged on onions, giving them their current appearance. They hail from an area famed for its outstanding alliums and spread throughout the land as business boomed.

Name: Orc
Trivia: These boar-ish brutes are far from boorish. Though most are soldiers by trade, some come to tire of the bloodshed and long to pursue careers as poets or painters instead.

Name: Ornery Onion
Trivia: Odious alliums possessed by evil spirits. Getting sprayed with their bodily juices only ever ends in tears.

Name: Piña Marauder
Trivia: Fructiform freaks that pose as pineapples, turning the tables on unsuspecting fruitarians in search of a tropical treat.

Name: Platypunk
Trivia: Don't be fooled<-->their goofy looks hide a serious mean streak. These wise guys might just make you an offer you can't refuse.

Name: Platypup
Trivia: Don't let the adorable yaps of these fluffy dog-duck things mislead you<--->their bills can break boulders. They can often be found furiously scratching their own bellies.

Name: Pocus Poppet
Trivia: Clay figures magically invested with minds of their own. In ancient times, they were used in dark rituals to summon up powerful spirits of the dead.

Name: Powie Yowie
Trivia: Shaggy-haired horrors at home in colder climates. They love an occasional dip in a hot spring, but when their fur is wet and slicked down you'll soon see they're thin as rakes.

Name: Prestidigitator
Trivia: Insatiable greed for mystical power left these malign mages steeped in malevolence. Unable to reliably retain human form, they cloak their protean persons in robes.

Name: Pteranodon
Trivia: Highly adaptable to changing conditions, these flying reptiles have endured since the primeval past. Some of the very earliest writings contain references to their airborne antics.

Name: Putrefido
Trivia: Cadaverous canines brought back to life by a pernicious power after expiring of exhaustion. Sadly, any smarts they once had did not make the return journey.

Name: Raptile
Trivia: Lovable lizards with genial grins. They're said to bring good luck, leading some monster wranglers to place them at the gates of their houses.

Name: Restless Armour
Trivia: The souls of soldiers slaughtered by monsters, fighting on in the armour they wore in life. Tragically, they don't even realize they're dead.

Name: Robber Rabbit
Trivia: Cottontails with a criminal tendency to pilfer farmers' produce. Their identity-concealing masks are family <6>harelooms<9> passed down from one generation to the next.

Name: Ruff Ruffian
Trivia: Werewolves that pose as bandits. When the moon is full, they get the munchies for man-flesh<--->preferably living.

Name: Sacksquatch
Trivia: Sacks of sand left on construction sites that eventually sprung to life. They love to play pranks, particularly ones that involve sprinkling sand where it's least wanted.

Name: Scallop Slime
Trivia: These splendid slimes spend so much time clammed up inside their shells they grow as hard and shiny as pearls.

Name: Scarfish
Trivia: Fishy stars that enliven the summer seaside with their bright colours. They prefer to stay underwater, but if feeling unsure of their security, they walk ashore assuredly on two legs.

Name: Scorpion
Trivia: Natural enemies of the cactiball, these desert assassins submerge themselves in the sand waiting to paralyse passing travellers with their venomous stingers.

Name: Seasaur
Trivia: These tyrants of the open seas have sent more humans to a watery end than they can count. When their distinctive cry rings out, even the crustiest captain turns tail and sails for home port.

Name: See Urchin
Trivia: This cowardly creature flees the second it senses danger, with no concern for the fate of any companions. Few monsters see eye to eye with them on this issue.

Name: Shadow
Trivia: Born in the unfathomable depths of darkness, these monsters are masters at mimicry. They've shadowed so many others that they've forgotten how they really look.

Name: Sham Hatwitch
Trivia: Boarish beasts that set out on journeys of personal discovery to overcome their cowardice. Though they say they're making progress, they still hide behind the broad brims of their beloved headwear when possible.

Name: Shell Slime
Trivia: Slimes that simply love spiral shells. These gloopy go-getters never stop growing, so they're always on the hunt for the perfect shell to squeeze into.

Name: She-Slime
Trivia: These slimes are proud of their quirky colouration, which is likely a genetic fluke. They feel faintly warm to the touch.

Name: Skeleton
Trivia: These unfortunate undead are responsibly recycled from the bodies of fallen soldiers, then worked to the bone.

Name: Skipper
Trivia: The unholy union of an abandoned boot and a furball fiend<--->a surefire recipe for a ripe aroma. Best keep your distance.

Name: Skullrider
Trivia: These scary swordsmen scurry across the land atop their skeletal steeds. They can sometimes be found racing against chariot chappies, their eternal rivals.

Name: Sky Fry
Trivia: These newborn clouds are eager to take their place as fully fledged formations in the aerial order. They may be small, but they never stop practicing their windy blasts.

Name: Slime
Trivia: Adored by all for its flexy physique and funny face, this little monster is something of an icon. Who wouldn't want one for a pal?

Name: Slime Knight
Trivia: These pint-sized slime chevaliers cannot abide dishonourable deeds. They patrol the land atop their slippery steeds to ensure no harm befalls slimekind.

Name: Slime Stack
Trivia: Three fast friends who decided to see how things stacked up when they stuck closer together. They're currently training to one day become a king slime.

Name: Small Fry
Trivia: Cheeky dragon hatchlings, or so it's commonly thought. They may well be full-grown, but no one knows who their parents are, so the truth remains unclear.

Name: Smog
Trivia: These murky amalgamations are the unquiet spirits of travellers who died deep in the mountains. They descend like mist to give victims a taste of what they suffered themselves.

Name: Snail Slime
Trivia: The spiral shells shouldered by these slimes grow as they age. Some say they've seen shells so sizable that a human could live inside one.

Name: Snowmangler
Trivia: A snowy slime that could pass as a regular snowman. When they melt, flights of angel slimes appear to welcome their newly defrosted souls.

Name: Soft Serve Spook
Trivia: This fuzzy fellow is often pounced upon by monsters looking for a sweet treat, but the joke's on them<--->one lick is all it takes to discover that it's saltier than smoked sardines.

Name: Stark Raven
Trivia: These creepy corvids can often be seen scooping up skulls from ancient battlefields. Their fledglings use the eye sockets to hide from predators.

Name: String Fella
Trivia: Ropey rapscallions prone to bouts of despondency unless tangled up in someone else's business. Afraid of a frayed knot, they feel the need to replace their string regularly.

Name: Stump Chump
Trivia: The remains of chopped-down trees driven by resentment at the humans who felled them. Travellers foolish enough to sit on their heads are slowly drained of their nutrients until only only a bag of bones remains.

Name: Succubat
Trivia: Charming and coquettish, these bat beasts prowl the trails by night, eyes aglow as they tempt travellers into their cruel embrace.

Name: Suckling Ocker
Trivia: These octopodal anomalies are thought to be mutated octopi, but when seared with a well-timed blast of fiery breath they start to smell more like squid.

Name: Swarmtroop
Trivia: A mind-boggling mass of insectoids that epitomise the concept of a hive mind. Each one has its own name, but no one can remember them all.

Name: Teeny Sanguini
Trivia: Baby demons known for their distinctive bovine markings. Considered fully grown once the black fur grows out and is replaced by a ravishing shade of rose pink.

Name: Toady
Trivia: These ample amphibians might have mutated into mega-sized monsters, but they retain their love for croaking out a tune. They like to put on evening concerts just after the rain lets up.

Name: Tongue Fu Fighter
Trivia: Curious creatures that will literally lick anything they like the look of. As such, they find it rather difficult to make friends, and lap up lashings of sweet nectar to alleviate their loneliness.

Name: Treeface
Trivia: Ancient trees, well over a thousand years old, possessed by wicked spirits. They will stupefy any who stray into their demesne, condemning unwary wanderers to walk the woods lost, never to return home.

Name: Urnexpected
Trivia: Travellers who peer inside these pots are put on the spot and ordered to say something funny. Luckily, they get the giggles at even the most groan-worthy jokes, so if you want that laugh, you don't really have to urn it.

Name: Ursa Major
Trivia: Wild bears brimming with malice. Their territorial disputes can get seriously grisly, sending other monsters fleeing from the forest in their droves.

Name: Vampire Cat
Trivia: Feline fiends that flit through gloomy skies. If you catch one grooming itself, it usually means rain is on the way.

Name: Vegandragora
Trivia: Dragons that live in harmony with herbs and flowers. They love nothing more than basking in the sun and will get together to lap up the rays on summer days.

Name: Walking Corpse
Trivia: Lost souls that wander the world in decaying prisons of flesh, tortured by the question of whether they're alive or dead.

Name: Warhog
Trivia: These intrepid infantryhogs are famed for their wild war cries. Once they have their foes trembling with fear, they unleash their full fury with savage slashes from their swords.

Name: Wax Murderer
Trivia: Tallowy toughs taken off castle walls and brought to life by mages with an unhealthy sense of humour.

Name: Weartiger
Trivia: These enigmatic individuals like to don tiger skins and leering grins. When they know their time is nearly up, they quietly slip away and hide.

Name: Will-o'-the-Whips
Trivia: These sneering spirits can insinuate their slender, supple bodies into the most cramped of crannies, ready to lash out when prey passes by.

Name: Wing Slime
Trivia: Slimes that sprouted wings to make dreams of soaring through the sky come true. Their wings double as a snug sleeping bag at night.

Name: Winky
Trivia: Clocking in at over 50% eyeball, these ocular oddities have a soft spot for children. When they get angry, their eyes turn red and they grow in strength.

Name: Woebergine
Trivia: These adorable vegetable-based monsters are proud of their ability to cut some rug. Any traveller straying into their terrain should be prepared to see them strut their stuff.
